hints: Resolve along smooth plane $P$ for particle $A$: $T = 2g\sin 10^\circ$.
Resolve along rough plane $Q$ for particle $B$: since $3g\sin 20^\circ > T$, particle $B$ tends to slide down, so friction acts up plane $Q$: $3g\sin 20^\circ = T + F$.
Resolve perpendicular to plane $Q$ to find normal reaction $R = 3g\cos 20^\circ$, and use $\mu = \frac{F}{R}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces parallel to smooth plane $P$ for particle $A$ ($m_A = 2\text{ kg}$) with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T = 2g\sin 10^\circ = 20\sin 10^\circ \approx 3.4730\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to rough plane $Q$ for particle $B$ ($m_B = 3\text{ kg}$):
$$R = 3g\cos 20^\circ = 30\cos 20^\circ \approx 28.1908\text{ N}$$

Compare forces parallel to plane $Q$: the component of weight down the plane is $3g\sin 20^\circ = 30\sin 20^\circ \approx 10.2606\text{ N}$, which exceeds $T$. Hence limiting friction acts up the plane:
$$3g\sin 20^\circ = T + F$$
$$F = 30\sin 20^\circ - 20\sin 10^\circ \approx 10.2606 - 3.4730 = 6.7876\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Analyze the equilibrium of the two connected particles on the double incline:

1. Particle $A$ on smooth plane $P$ (inclined at $10^\circ$):
Since plane $P$ is smooth, no friction acts on $A$. Resolve along plane $P$:
$$T = m_A g\sin 10^\circ = 2 \times 10 \times \sin 10^\circ = 20\sin 10^\circ \approx 3.47296\text{ N}$$

2. Particle $B$ on rough plane $Q$ (inclined at $20^\circ$):
Resolve perpendicular to plane $Q$:
$$R = m_B g\cos 20^\circ = 3 \times 10 \times \cos 20^\circ = 30\cos 20^\circ \approx 28.1908\text{ N}$$

3. Determine the direction of friction on $B$:
The component of weight pulling $B$ down plane $Q$ is $30\sin 20^\circ \approx 10.2606\text{ N}$.
Because this downward gravitational pull ($10.2606\text{ N}$) is greater than the tension holding it back ($3.4730\text{ N}$), particle $B$ tends to slide downwards. Therefore, friction $F$ acts upwards along plane $Q$:
$$3g\sin 20^\circ = T + F$$
$$F = 3g\sin 20^\circ - T = 30\sin 20^\circ - 20\sin 10^\circ$$
$$F \approx 10.2606 - 3.4730 = 6.7876\text{ N}$$

hints: Apply Newton's second law to the smooth system: $3g\sin 20^\circ - 2g\sin 10^\circ = (3 + 2)a$ to find acceleration $a$.
If each particle moves a distance $x$ along its incline, $B$ descends vertically by $x\sin 20^\circ$ and $A$ ascends vertically by $x\sin 10^\circ$.
Set the total difference in heights equal to $1\text{ m}$: $x(\sin 10^\circ + \sin 20^\circ) = 1$, find $x$, then use $x = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to find time $t$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the two-particle system along the string:
$$3g\sin 20^\circ - 2g\sin 10^\circ = (2 + 3)a$$
$$30\sin 20^\circ - 20\sin 10^\circ = 5a$$
$$10.2606 - 3.4730 = 5a$$
$$5a = 6.7876 \implies a = \frac{6.7876}{5} = 1.35753\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Let $x$ be the distance moved by each particle along its plane. The difference in vertical heights is:
$$\Delta h = x\sin 10^\circ + x\sin 20^\circ = x(\sin 10^\circ + \sin 20^\circ)$$
Set $\Delta h = 1\text{ m}$:
$$x = \frac{1}{\sin 10^\circ + \sin 20^\circ} = \frac{1}{0.173648 + 0.342020} = \frac{1}{0.515668} \approx 1.93923\text{ m}$$

Use the constant-acceleration formula $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$:
$$x = \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
$$1.93923 = \frac{1}{2}(1.35753)t^2 = 0.678765 t^2$$
$$t^2 = \frac{1.93923}{0.678765} \approx 2.8570$$
$$t = \sqrt{2.8570} \approx 1.69\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Finds $a = 1.358\text{ m s}^{-2}$, forms $x(\sin 10^\circ + \sin 20^\circ) = 1$, and uses $x = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to find $t = 1.69\text{ s}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
1. Calculate the system acceleration with both planes smooth:
Write Newton's second law for $B$ moving down plane $Q$:
$$3g\sin 20^\circ - T = 3a$$
Write Newton's second law for $A$ moving up plane $P$:
$$T - 2g\sin 10^\circ = 2a$$
Add both equations to eliminate the internal tension $T$:
$$3g\sin 20^\circ - 2g\sin 10^\circ = (3 + 2)a = 5a$$
Substitute $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$5a = 30\sin 20^\circ - 20\sin 10^\circ$$
$$5a = 10.2606 - 3.4730 = 6.7876$$
Divide by $5$:
$$a = \frac{6.7876}{5} = 1.35753\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

2. Relate the distance travelled along the planes to the difference in vertical height:
Initially, both particles are at the exact same horizontal level.
When the string moves a distance $x$:
Particle $A$ moves a distance $x$ up plane $P$ ($10^\circ$ to horizontal), rising by height:
$$h_A = x\sin 10^\circ$$
Particle $B$ moves a distance $x$ down plane $Q$ ($20^\circ$ to horizontal), descending by height:
$$h_B = x\sin 20^\circ$$
The difference in vertical height between the two particles is the sum of these changes:
$$\Delta h = h_A + h_B = x\sin 10^\circ + x\sin 20^\circ = x(\sin 10^\circ + \sin 20^\circ)$$

3. Find the required distance $x$ when $\Delta h = 1\text{ m}$:
$$x(\sin 10^\circ + \sin 20^\circ) = 1$$
$$x = \frac{1}{\sin 10^\circ + \sin 20^\circ} = \frac{1}{0.173648 + 0.342020} = \frac{1}{0.515668} \approx 1.93923\text{ m}$$

4. Calculate the time $t$ taken to travel this distance from rest ($u = 0$):
$$x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
$$1.93923 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(1.35753)t^2$$
$$1.93923 = 0.678765 t^2$$
Divide by $0.678765$:
$$t^2 = \frac{1.93923}{0.678765} \approx 2.8570$$
Take the square root:
$$t = \sqrt{2.8570} \approx 1.69\text{ s}$$
